race_context: Concord Community Schools is in Elkhart, Indiana. It has seven schools: Concord High School, Concord Junior High, Concord Intermediate and four elementary schools (East Side, Ox Bow, South Side and West Side). The superintendent is Dan Funston {ccs_leadership}.
Federal (NCES) data show 5,212 students enrolled in 2024-25, down from 5,288 in 2023-24 and 5,348 in 2022-23 {plain_ccs}.

The board has five members. Each is elected to a four-year term and must live within the school corporation's boundaries. Current members: Jennifer Davis (president, term 2022-2026), Tim Yoder (vice president, 2025-2028), Tara Towner (secretary, 2022-2026), Mike Malooley (2022-2026) and Tim Koontz (2025-2028) {ccs_board}.

How seats are elected: in 2022 three seats were filled from one pool of eight candidates. Candidates could live in any district, but no more than one could come from District 3 {gn_recount}. In 2024 two seats were on the ballot (Koontz, Yoder and Stacy McDowell ran, vote for not more than two) {gn_2024}{ccs_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the three seats won in 2022, held by Davis, Towner and Malooley, all of whose terms end in 2026 {ccs_board}{gn_recount}. All three are on the ballot for 'Elkhart Concord School Board, District 1' and no one else is listed {in_list}. The state list says 'vote for 1'. If the race fills all three expiring seats, as in 2022, all three incumbents would win. Voters should check the county sample ballot for the number to vote for {in_list}{gn_recount}.
The 2022 race was decided by a recount. Davis and Towner kept their seats. Malooley won the third seat by 55 votes over Stacy McDowell, replacing incumbent Jared Sponseller {gn_recount}.

Operating referendum: in a Nov. 2, 2021 special election, voters narrowly rejected renewing Concord's operating referendum, 1,514 (51.29%) to 1,438 (48.71%). The renewal would have cut the rate from 40.5 to 32 cents per $100 of assessed value. Funston said referendum money made up 10% of the overall budget {wvpe_ref21}. No later Concord referendum was found.

Facilities: in April 2025 the Elkhart Truth reported a multi-year renovation plan. Phase one covered Jake Field ($16.2 million), Ox Bow Elementary ($13.2 million) and South Side Elementary ($17.7 million), with high school cafeteria, classroom and activity-center work to follow. The article did not say how the work is funded {et_reno}.
In 2026 the board unanimously voted to rename the district office the George S. Dyer Education Center, after a longtime Concord educator and administrator {et_dyer}.
No reporting was found on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Concord's budget.
No 2026 Concord candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the race was found. Statements below come from the candidates' district board biographies and 2022 election coverage.

background: Corporate treasurer at Indiana Wood Products in Middlebury {ccs_davis}.
Parent of two Concord graduates. Has volunteered in classrooms and with SOAR, and is a past PTO president at Concord South Side Elementary {ccs_davis}.
Treasurer of the Well Foundation and a member of Tri Kappa {ccs_davis}.
First elected in November 2014 and took office in January 2015; now board president {ccs_davis}{ccs_board}.
Led the 2022 field after the recount with 2,264 votes {gn_recount}.

items: Her district biography quotes her: "Our state legislature places a lot of financial constraints on local school boards" {ccs_davis}.
After winning in 2022, the Elkhart Truth reported that she looked forward to improving the quality of education "while also being fiscally responsible for taxpayers" {et_2022}.
Her biography quotes her: "All children should have an opportunity to reach their full learning potential in a safe and caring environment" {ccs_davis}.

Purdue University bachelor's degree in industrial management {ccs_malooley}.
